name: Volta
tagline: Loud where it counts. Quiet everywhere else.

tokens.usage: Page ground. The default surface for everything.

tokens.name: paper-sunk
tokens.usage: Wells, code blocks, inactive tracks, table stripes.

tokens.name: line
tokens.usage: Hairline dividers and quiet borders. Never the sole edge of a control.

tokens.name: edge

tokens.name: ink

idea_headline: A risograph print of a dashboard.
idea: Paper-and-ink calm everywhere, then one hit of electric vermilion exactly where the eye should land. Hard edges, hard shadows, no blur, no gradients. Volta is for data products that refuse to be beige: the restraint is what makes the one loud thing land.
use_for: Analytics products, operational dashboards, pricing and launch pages, anything where one number or one action must dominate a busy screen.
avoid_when: Long reading (the hard edges tire over 800 words), luxury or institutional subjects, and anything that needs more than one loud element per view.
principles_headline: Five rules, and the first one is the system.
principles: Volt marks the primary action or the number that matters. If two things are volt, neither is.
Figures are set in the mono numeral role: tabular, big, never decorative. Text explains; the number carries.
Separation comes from the 2px edge and the hard offset shadow. There is no blur anywhere in the system.
Only interactive things cast a shadow. Static cards are flat on the paper.
Zero radius for containers, 4px for controls, a pill only for things that move (switches) or pulse (status dots).
voice: Plain, short, specific. Lead with the fact, then the meaning: "Annual plans drove 70% of growth."
Sentence case everywhere; uppercase only through the label style.
Errors are fixes: "No table called orderz. Did you mean orders?" Never "Something went wrong."
Second person, no exclamation marks, no emoji.
colour_headline: Three paper grounds, one ink, one volt.
colour_note: Two themes: Paper (light, first and fallback) and Night. In Night the hard shadow turns volt, so interactive things glow. Volt is a fill only (2.9:1 on paper); volt as text is volt-ink. Status never relies on colour alone: always a word, a ▲/▼ or a glyph.
chart_note: The focal series is always cobalt; volt is the comparison; the neutral third series is ink-muted. Series are ordered by lightness so they stay distinct without hue.
type_headline: Bricolage shouts, Instrument explains, JetBrains counts.
type_note: Three Google-hosted families. Display is Bricolage Grotesque at 800 and 700 with tight tracking and tight leading; one display-xl per page at most. Instrument Sans carries reading and UI. JetBrains Mono carries every figure.
space_headline: A 4px base, a 2px edge, a 4px shadow.
space: Gaps inside controls; the hard-shadow offset on cards.
Gaps between cards so hard shadows never touch.
edges: Cards, callouts, tables, cover blocks. Square by default.
Switch tracks, status dots. The only round thing: it signals "this moves".
Every control and interactive card has a 2px edge in the edge colour. The hairline is decorative only.
depth: 4px 4px 0 edge. Buttons and interactive cards at rest. In Night it is volt.
The shadow collapses as the element moves into it (80ms ease-out).
A 2px paper gap, then 2px solid cobalt. Every control; never removed.
Fast and physical. Hover lifts 2px; press drives into the shadow; the switch thumb overshoots, the only bounce. No fade longer than 160ms.
components_headline: The kit wears the tokens; the edge and shadow are yours to add.
components_note: Kit components take Volta through the contract: paper grounds, volt primary, cobalt ring, 4px radius. The signature hard edge and offset shadow are classes you put on authored elements: v-hard on a card, v-btn on a button.
buttons: <Button>Run query</Button><Button variant="secondary">Save view</Button><Button variant="outline">Export</Button><Button variant="ghost">Cancel</Button><button className="v-btn v-btn-primary">Run query</button><button className="v-btn v-btn-acid">Ask Volta</button><button className="v-btn">Export</button>
buttons_note: Kit buttons on the left; authored v-btn on the right with the 2px edge and hard shadow. One primary per view. Acid is reserved for AI-assisted actions, never destructive ones.
tags: VoltSelectedDraftFailedNew▲ 12%StaleInfo
tags_note: Tags are the label role in caps. Status tags carry a glyph or a word with the colour, never colour alone.
fields_note: Fields sit on paper-raised with the 2px edge; the focus ring is cobalt with a paper gap. Labels are the label role above the field.
stats:
Revenue▲ 12% vs last week
Annual plansof growth
stats_note: Stat is a label, a big mono numeral and a delta with a ▲/▼ glyph. One accented Stat per row, for the number that matters most. Figures come from data, never typed.
callouts:
No table called orderzDid you mean orders?
Cobalt means information. A hint about the data, not an alarm.
Saved. Your view is shared with the team.
Query timed out after 5s. Add a date filter and run it again.
callouts_note: A callout states the fact, then the fix. Status grounds are the soft tokens; the text stays ink.
chart_comp_note: Charts take the chart tokens in order: cobalt first, volt for the comparison. No gradient fills; direct labels where they fit.
table_note: Tables are ink on paper with hairline rows and mono figures; the hard edge belongs to the container, not to each cell.
card:
Insight

Annual plans drove 70% of growth

Monthly plans added 1,120 customers but 410 churned inside 90 days. Annual plans added 640 and kept 612. Reorder the pricing page.
card_note: An interactive card casts shadow-hard-lg and lifts on hover; a static card is flat with a hairline. Card titles are the title role.
motifs_headline: Stripes, slabs, and the misregistered print.
motifs_note: Volta draws with flat blocks and a 4px stripe screen, like a two-colour riso print whose plates slipped by one shadow. Use one device per page, and let the data live inside it.

motifs.title: The stripe screen
motifs.usage: A 4px edge stripe at a 16px pitch, clipped inside a block. Use it as the texture of a selected or pending region, or as a bar fill for the "unknown" share.

motifs.title: The split bar
motifs.usage: One number split into its parts as a single bar with hard edges: 240 + 160, annual against monthly. Label every segment inside it; no legend.

motifs.title: The status dot
motifs.usage: The one round thing. A volt dot pulses for live, a positive dot for healthy, an ink dot for idle; each sits next to a word.

sample_note: A product analytics opening: the finding as a headline, one volt number, the comparison in cobalt, and a ledger below. Everything else is paper.
sample:
Volta analytics · Weekly reviewSynthetic data · 2 Oct 2026

Annual plans drove 70% of growth.

Monthly plans add more customers and lose most of them inside a quarter. The pricing page still leads with monthly.

Revenue, 90 days▲ 12% vs prior
New customers1,120 monthly · 640 annual
Kept at 90 days▼ 4 pts vs prior

Revenue by plan, weekly

Cohorts
dos: Figures in the numeral role, tabular.
Hard 2px edges and offset shadows on anything you can click.
Let the finding be the headline; put the number next to it in volt.
donts: No blur, no gradients, no soft shadows.
No volt as text on paper; use volt-ink.
No two primaries side by side.
No rounded cards; radius is 0 for containers.
binding_losses: The hard edge as distinct from the hairline, the acid highlighter, the soft status grounds and raised versus sunk paper have no contract slot. They are carried as --ds-* properties and the v-* classes above; kit components follow ink and paper but not the hard edge.
footer: Paper first, Night second. Fonts: Bricolage Grotesque 700/800, Instrument Sans 400/500/600, JetBrains Mono 400–700, all Google-hosted.

queries.series: select week, plan, revenue from rows order by week, plan
queries.table: select plan, sum(customers) as customers, sum(kept) as kept, round(100.0*sum(kept)/sum(customers)) as kept_pct from rows group by plan order by customers desc
queries.totals: select sum(revenue) as revenue, sum(customers) as customers, round(100.0*sum(kept)/sum(customers)) as kept_pct, 70 as annual_share from rows

data.tab_body: Overview: the finding, the number, the comparison.

hand.headline: Flat blocks, a 2px edge, one slipped shadow.
hand.note: Volta draws like a two-colour riso print: flat fills in volt and cobalt, a square-capped 2px edge in ink, and a hard shadow offset by 6px as if the second plate slipped. No gradients, no rounded strokes, no texture except the stripe screen. The subject is whatever the artifact is about; the hand is this.
rules: 2px ink, square caps, square joins. Every shape has it.
Flat volt or cobalt; sunk paper for the quiet parts.
6px hard offset in ink (volt in Night). Only on the main body of the drawing.
The 4px stripe screen, clipped inside a block, for pending or unknown regions.
Mono caps at 11px for labels; the display face for the one number.
A drawing may lift 2px on hover; it never fades in.

motion: Interactive things lift 2px and the shadow grows by 2px, 80ms ease-out.
The element drives into its shadow: translate 4px, shadow 0. 80ms.
A 2px paper gap then 2px cobalt. Never removed.
Sections use the kit reveal-up with 120ms stagger; nothing longer than 400ms.
One ambient loop per page at most: the live status dot pulses. No marquee.
Bars grow from the baseline on first paint; no easing longer than 300ms.

tpl.slide_body: Of every 100 new customers, this many are still paying at day 90. Annual cohorts keep 96 of 100.
tpl.ed_headline: The plan that kept its customers
tpl.ed_deck: Monthly plans bring the crowd. Annual plans keep it. A quarter of synthetic numbers on why the pricing page should lead with the one that stays.
tpl.ed_byline: By the analytics team · 2 Oct 2026 · 6 min read
tpl.ed_body: Monthly plans added 1,120 customers in ninety days and lost 410 of them before the quarter ended. Annual plans added 640 and kept 612. The pricing page still leads with monthly, because that is what every pricing page does. The numbers say the opposite order would have kept more people.
steps: Sixty pick monthly, forty pick annual. Each square is one customer; the colour is the plan.
The monthly squares thin out: 37 of the 60 remain. The annual block is nearly whole.

tpl.landing_headline: Ask a question. Get the number.
tpl.landing_sub: Plain-words questions over your warehouse, answered with a chart and the SQL that made it. No dashboards to build first.
features: The figure leads; the chart explains it; the SQL is one click away.
Every answer marks the number that matters and nothing else.
Postgres, BigQuery, Snowflake. Read-only, in your region.
